content: A tablespoon is a type of spoon primarily used for serving food or measuring ingredients in cooking. In English, the tablespoon is commonly abbreviated as T, tbs, or Tbsp, while in German and Dutch, it is abbreviated as EL, derived from the words Esslöffel and Eetlepel, respectively. However, in Australia, one tablespoon is defined as 20 milliliters. When measuring solid ingredients, such as granulated sugar, the contents should be leveled off to the flat surface of the spoon. This is in contrast to a heaping tablespoon, which refers to the maximum amount that can be held in the spoon. Relationship to Teaspoon In most regions, one tablespoon is equivalent to three teaspoons. However, in Australia, one tablespoon equals four teaspoons. In some parts of Asia, a tablespoon is equivalent to only two teaspoons. Historical Definitions Historically, the United States defined a tablespoon as half of a fluid ounce.S. Despite this, the relationship between a tablespoon and half a fluid ounce remains accurate. Tablespoons can still be used as a practical tool for measuring ingredients when other measuring devices are unavailable.
